item.title: Copper's worst day since April 2025: a fall of nearly 6 per cent on Wednesday wipes out the metal's November gains and leaves the price close to where the year began
item.description: Copper lost close to 6 per cent on Wednesday 18 November, its steepest one-day fall since April 2025, before steadying on Thursday, according to bank commentary carried by Zambia Monitor and an analysis by the broker XTB. The metal is down roughly 12 to 13 per cent in November and trades near US$12,560 a tonne, about where it started 2026. For Zambia, whose kwacha slipped to just under K20.50 to the dollar last week, the question is whether September's record highs were the peak.

item.title: 09:30 at the High Court: Judge Geoffrey Mulenga rules today on whether Mundubile and Zulu's sedition bail plea can be heard in Lusaka, as Mpika North's MP keeps his seat
item.description: The Lusaka High Court is due at 09:30 this morning to rule on the Director of Public Prosecutions' objection that Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu's bail application in their sedition case is in the wrong court, the Daily Nation and the Zambian Observer reported on Thursday. A three-judge panel rules on Tuesday 24 November on constitutional bail for all 18 treason accused. Separately, the Daily Nation reports that Judge Catherine Lombe has upheld Francis Kapyanga's election in Mpika North, and that judgment is pending in the Lima petition.

item.title: 'You can't make law for one man': Kabimba joins the term-limits argument, Harrington says the Speaker should not preside, and Chapter One demands reasons for the march ban
item.description: Economic Front leader Wynter Kabimba told Prime Television that the law is not made for one man, the Zambian Observer reported on Thursday, as the Daily Nation carried William Harrington's argument that Speaker Nelly Mutti, who sat on the Mung'omba commission that rejected a third term, should recuse herself from any term-limits debate. Chapter One Foundation gave police until Thursday to give specific reasons for advising against the 25 November marches. The Observer also reports Saviour Chishimba's apology for campaigning for the UPND Alliance.

item.title: US$105 million through Zanaco for small firms, and a K5 billion State guarantee scheme in the 2027 Budget: Katotobwe asks that the money reach businesses that can use it
item.description: Four development lenders and Citi have put together a US$105 million facility to be lent through Zanaco to small and medium-sized enterprises, with Swedfund and FinDev Canada providing US$35 million each, Norfund US$25 million and Citi US$10 million, Zambia Monitor and the pan-African outlet Afrimag reported after the signing in Lusaka on Wednesday 18 November. Trade and Exports Minister Caroline Katotobwe used the occasion to point to the 2027 Budget's K5 billion Small-Business Guarantee Scheme and a planned development finance institution.

item.title: Seventy-one per cent of the market: Sialubalo orders a national crackdown on illicit alcohol, as Zambian Breweries links 43 per cent of Chainama admissions to illicit drink
item.description: Local Government Minister Gift Sialubalo has directed enforcement agencies to step up inspections of unlicensed liquor outlets, dismantle illegal manufacturing and distribution networks and tighten border surveillance, telling a liquor enforcement conference in Lusaka on Wednesday 18 November that illicit alcohol is estimated at 71 per cent of Zambia's market, Zambia Monitor and the Daily Nation report. Zambian Breweries' managing director said 43 per cent of psychiatric admissions at Chainama Hills Hospital were linked to high-strength illicit alcohol.

item.title: Four deaths in a day and 82 new suspected cases: the cholera toll reaches 75 as the count passes 3,250, and Mpongwe opens a treatment centre with 26 patients
item.description: Zambia recorded 82 new suspected cholera cases and four deaths in 24 hours, News Diggers reported on Thursday 19 November, citing the Zambia National Public Health Institute: 3,258 suspected cases since the outbreak was declared on 28 July, 464 of them confirmed, 75 deaths, 98 patients in hospital and 3,085 discharged. Three days earlier Zambia Monitor had reported 3,099 cases, 68 deaths and 27 districts affected across seven provinces. On the Copperbelt, Mpongwe's district health director said a dedicated centre was treating 26 patients.

item.title: A guard of honour and a goal inside a minute: ZESCO United send captain Lindo Mkhonta off with a 2–1 win over Red Arrows, as Napsa, Chirundu and Kabwe Warriors win late
item.description: Lindo Mkhonta's last match for ZESCO United ended in a 2–1 win over Red Arrows at Trade Fair Grounds in Ndola on Thursday 19 November, ZamFoot reported: Luka Mutoshi headed in inside the first minute, Kelvin Kampamba's cross went in off a defender in the 53rd, and Jonathan Manda replied for Arrows in the 71st. Elsewhere in matchweek eight of the MTN Super League transitional season, Napsa Stars beat Makeni All Stars 2–1 with a stoppage-time winner, Chirundu United won 1–0 at Roan United in the 92nd minute and Kabwe Warriors won 1–0 at Mufulira Wanderers.

item.title: Nigeria in March for the under-23s after a 4–0 comeback over DR Congo, and Denmark recall Nadia Nadim, 38, for the Copper Queens friendly in Esbjerg on 5 December
item.description: Zambia's under-23s will play Nigeria over two legs in March 2027 for a place at the Egypt 2027 U-23 Africa Cup of Nations, after Nigeria overturned a 2–0 first-leg deficit with a 4–0 win over DR Congo in Ikenne on Tuesday 17 November, ZamFoot reported. The tournament doubles as the road to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The Copper Queens, meanwhile, learned on Thursday that Denmark have recalled striker Nadia Nadim, 108 caps and 38 goals, for their friendly in Esbjerg on 5 December.

item.title: 'Must immediately release the eighteen': Amnesty International asks Hichilema to free the treason detainees, ahead of High Court rulings on their liberty on 20 and 24 November
item.description: In an Urgent Action dated Tuesday 17 November, Amnesty International asked President Hakainde Hichilema to release Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others detained since the August election, saying they were held 16 days without charge, denied timely access to courts, lawyers and family, and allegedly tortured. Reported by Zambia Monitor and the Zambian Observer on Wednesday, the appeal lands as the High Court prepares rulings on 20 and 24 November. Spokesperson Elvis Nkandu told News Diggers the government does not control judges.

item.title: Reasons and another date, or an appeal to the minister: the anti-third-term consortium invokes a 2014 ruling against the police advice, as a priest, an analyst and Lubinda weigh in
item.description: The civil society groups told not to march on 25 November say they will test the police advice against the 2014 LAZ v Attorney General ruling, which requires the police to give reasons and propose another date, and will appeal to the Home Affairs Minister if no date is offered by Thursday 19 November, former LAZ president Linda Kasonde said in a statement carried by the Zambian Observer. George Chulumanda called the advice 'dictatorship in uniform'; analyst Neo Simutanyi told News Diggers the UPND should groom a successor.

item.title: 'Housekeeper and personal assistant': former ambassador Martha Mwitumwa petitions the High Court over her treason arrest and an August 'abduction', saying she was held four days
item.description: Martha Lungu Mwitumwa, 59, formerly ambassador to Switzerland, has asked the Lusaka High Court to order her immediate release, arguing that her treason arrest this month and what she calls an abduction in August breached her constitutional rights, News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report. The petition names the Attorney General and says she was held four days in August and questioned about Brian Mundubile, for whom she says she worked only as housekeeper and personal assistant. Police charged her on 9 November with plotting to usurp executive power.

item.title: K30,000 each or nine months: David Kazadi and Mwaka Halwindi are convicted under a plea agreement in the obscene material case, as the producer apologises and cites counselling
item.description: Film producer David Kazadi, 34, and Mwaka Halwindi, 23, pleaded guilty under a plea agreement and were each fined K30,000, payable by Tuesday 1 December, with nine months' imprisonment in default, the Zambian Observer reported on Wednesday 18 November. The deal, struck under the Plea Negotiations and Agreements Act, was disclosed to Lusaka magistrate Kawama Mwamfuli on 10 November, Zambia Monitor reported. Kazadi said on Facebook that an apology alone could not undo what had happened and that he had undergone counselling, News Diggers reported.

item.title: 'We are scared of foreign investments': in Kitwe, Musokotwane says fear of outside capital holds Africa back, and defends the IMF as a US$1.47 billion deal awaits approval
item.description: At the Copperbelt 2027 National Budget Symposium in Kitwe, Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane said that China, Japan and Germany grew by opening up to foreign investment and that investors create jobs for local firms rather than crowding them out, News Diggers reported on Wednesday 18 November. The Zambian Observer reported him saying mineral wealth is no reason to leave the IMF, whose 191 members include Saudi Arabia, after Zambia's US$1.7 billion facility closed in January and a new US$1.472 billion arrangement reached staff level in October.

item.title: 'Not conditional on any commercial agreements': US Democrats plan probes into Africa minerals deals from January, with the reported threat to Zambia's HIV aid at the centre
item.description: Democrats preparing to take control of the US House of Representatives in January say they will open formal investigations into the Trump administration's critical-minerals agreements in Africa, Semafor reported, in a story that reached Zambian readers through the Zambian Observer on Wednesday 18 November. Among their grievances is a March report that the State Department threatened to withhold HIV assistance to push Zambia into a minerals deal. A State Department spokesperson said US health assistance is not conditional on any commercial agreement.

item.title: Thirty-five boys, twenty places and a group with Zimbabwe and Eswatini: Chris Kaunda opens the under-17 camp for Maputo, as Fashion Sakala's parting shot at bloggers resurfaces
item.description: Under-17 coach Chris Kaunda has called 35 players into camp in Lusaka ahead of the CAF Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations COSAFA qualifier in Maputo from 4 to 13 December, where Zambia are drawn with Zimbabwe and Eswatini in Group C and only three COSAFA sides reach the finals in Morocco, ZamFoot and News Diggers report. The squad, including two under-15 strikers who helped win Tier B of the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, will be cut to 20. A file video of Fashion Sakala saying bloggers turned on him when he refused to pay them is circulating.

item.title: K2 million from KCM for the Ngoma Awards on 10 December, and Yo Maps everywhere at the Kwacha Music Awards on 27 November: Zambia's two big nights of the year take shape
item.description: Konkola Copper Mines has put K2 million into the 2026 Ngoma Awards, the National Arts Council's flagship honours since 1997, to be handed out on 10 December, Zambian Music Blog reported on Wednesday 18 November; Culture and Arts Minister Christopher Chibuye called it an important show of support for the arts. Two weeks earlier, on Friday 27 November, the 8th Sun FM Kwacha Music Awards fill the Mulungushi International Conference Centre, with Yo Maps carrying 13 nominations and Chile One, Chef 187, Mampi and Sampa the Great in the main categories.

item.title: 'Not to proceed': police cite intelligence in telling two consortiums to call off their 25 November term-limit marches, as Andeleki says there is nothing to protest
item.description: In a statement on Tuesday 17 November, police spokesperson Chipo Kaitisha said the service had reviewed notifications from two groups planning processions in Lusaka on Wednesday 25 November over presidential term limits and was advising both not to go ahead, citing intelligence gathered and the prevailing national security situation. One march was to defend the two-term limit, the other to call for its removal. Home Affairs Minister Clement Andeleki told News Diggers he expects no one to protest, because the President is not seeking a third term.

item.title: 'A difference between a third term and a term limit': the UPND answers Khama's 'last move' jibe, Ezra Tembo's NRPUP backs the status quo, AIPAC says a petition cannot do it alone
item.description: UPND media director Mark Simuuwe said on Tuesday that the proposal before Parliament would remove the ceiling on presidential terms rather than add a third, that voters should decide how long a leader stays, and that former Botswana president Ian Khama had misunderstood it. Khama had said at the weekend that Hichilema was making his last move to consolidate power without time limit. Leader of the Opposition Ezra Tembo said his party backs the current limit, and the Acton Institute said Article 79 cannot be sidestepped by a petition.

item.title: 'A commitment, not a wish list': ZCCM-IH plans US$2.7 billion over ten years to become a US$7 billion company, with 3,022 MW of power, more of Mingomba and US$704 million of debt
item.description: At its Shareholder Day in Lusaka on Monday 16 November, the State mining investor unveiled a 2026–2035 plan to lift its value from about US$1.2 billion to US$7 billion and annual revenue from US$211 million to US$738 million. It intends to raise its Mingomba stake from 20 to 25 per cent, build a 3,022 MW generation portfolio, open gold and manganese buying centres and ring-fence exploration money. Funding is planned, not secured: US$704 million of debt, US$300 million of equity and US$1–1.7 billion from partners, after a K4.92 billion group loss in 2025.

item.title: 'The signature begins the partnership, the results will give it meaning': Zambia and Malawi agree to stop testing the same goods twice, with a mutual recognition deal the next step
item.description: The Malawi Bureau of Standards and Zambia's three quality-infrastructure agencies signed a memorandum of understanding in Lusaka on Tuesday 17 November to cut the technical barriers that make traders certify products on both sides of the border. Trade Minister Caroline Katotobwe called it a milestone and asked for a results-oriented action plan; the Malawian side pressed for the mutual recognition arrangements that would let each country accept the other's test results. The World Bank-funded Southern Africa Trade and Connectivity Project backs the work.

item.title: Three borehole contractors barred for two years, 26 CDF projects faulted and a NATSAVE server tender sent back: the ZPPA's third-quarter report card
item.description: At its third-quarter briefing in Lusaka on Monday 16 November, the Zambia Public Procurement Authority said it had suspended Capricon Innovation, Nkanmu Investments and Totten Infrastructure from public tenders for two years after they failed to complete borehole work for the Ministry of Water Development and Sanitation. Director General Gloria Ngoma also reported irregular contract extensions and documentation lapses across 26 CDF projects in 11 councils, 19,664 tenders on the e-procurement system, and 18 bidder appeals, one of them at NATSAVE.

item.title: 'Commodity sovereignty is not an option': ground is broken on the ZAMVAX cholera vaccine plant in Lusaka South, as the outbreak it is meant to answer reaches 3,099 cases
item.description: Health Minister Roma Chilengi and China's Wang Sheng broke ground on Tuesday 17 November at the Lusaka South Multi-Facility Economic Zone for a plant that will fill, finish and pack up to 20 million oral cholera vaccine doses a year from imported bulk antigen. ZAMVAX is 60 per cent owned by the Industrial Development Corporation and 40 per cent by China's Jijia; phase one was costed at US$24.13 million within a US$213 million project signed on 2 November. The ZNPHI's 16 November update put the outbreak at 3,099 cases and 68 deaths.

item.title: No more adjournments: a Lusaka magistrate sets 16 December for Esther Lungu's theft trial to resume, more than a year after it last moved and 17 months after her husband's death
item.description: Resident Magistrate Mbuvywana Sinvula told the Lusaka Magistrates' Court on Monday 16 November that the case against the former First Lady and four co-accused, charged with the theft of three vehicles and a certificate of title between August 2021 and September 2022, had gone more than a year without reaching continued trial and would not be adjourned again, Kalemba reported. The matter returns on Wednesday 16 December. Esther Lungu has not attended since former president Edgar Lungu died on 5 June 2025; none of the allegations has been tested at trial.

item.title: An own goal rescues a point in Bujumbura, but Togo's 3–0 over Algeria drops Zambia to third: Group I now reads Algeria 7, Togo 6, Zambia 5 with two rounds left
item.description: Burundi led through substitute Bonfils-Caleb Bimenyimana late in the second half at Stade Intwari on Tuesday 17 November, a goal Zambia argued was offside, before Akbar Muderi turned Zephania Phiri's cross into his own net in the 85th minute for 1–1. The point was worth less than it looked: at the Stade de Kégué, Togo beat Algeria 3–0 with all three goals before half-time, two of them from Thibault Klidjé, and leapfrogged Zambia into second place.

item.title: 'I wore the jersey with pride': Fashion Sakala, 29, retires from international football hours after Bujumbura, nine years after a debut that ended in a red card
item.description: The Chipolopolo captain announced on his Facebook page on Tuesday 17 November that, after much reflection, he had decided to retire from international football, calling the captaincy among the proudest moments of his life. He made his senior debut against Algeria on 2 September 2017 and was sent off; he won the Africa U-20 Cup of Nations at home that year, scored against Portugal, Iran and Germany at the U-20 World Cup, hit a hat-trick against Mauritania in 2021 and went to the 2023 and 2025 Nations Cups. Outlets differ on his caps, 41 or 47.

item.title: Friday for jurisdiction, Tuesday for liberty: the High Court rules on 20 November whether it can hear Mundubile and Zulu's sedition bail plea, and on 24 November on bail for the 18
item.description: The Lusaka High Court heard the State's objection to the sedition bail application on Monday 16 November and reserved its ruling to Friday 20 November at 09:30. The Director of Public Prosecutions argued that filing in Lusaka while the case sat in Solwezi was an abuse of process; the defence relied on Section 123 of the Criminal Procedure Code. News Diggers reports that the separate constitutional bail application by all 18 treason accused will be decided on Tuesday 24 November, the day Mundubile and Zulu are also due to take plea before a magistrate.

item.title: The lawyers come in: LAZ says it will litigate if need be to keep the two-term limit, as a youth consortium sets a march on Parliament for 25 November and M'membe cries foul
item.description: News Diggers reports that Law Association of Zambia president Arnold Kaluba has pledged to defend Article 106's two-term limit, by litigation if necessary, and welcomed the Justice Minister's assurance that the Executive will not interfere with the petitions before Parliament. The same day the Zambian Observer carried the Zambia Youth Organisation Consortium's plan for a march from Northmead to Parliament on 25 November, and Fred M'membe's reply calling it neither spontaneous nor organic.

item.title: 'Mapanza should not be left behind': Hichilema promises a dam on the Munyeke and Ng'onga rivers for wheat, says Zambia has never been better, and gives a school over K1 million
item.description: On Sunday 15 November the President closed his Southern Province weekend at St Mark's in Mapanza, Mbabala Constituency. The Times of Zambia reports a promise of strategic dams, boreholes and health facilities; News Diggers reports his warning against social-media lies; a UPND Media Team account carried by the Zambian Observer names the rivers, a wheat ambition and the donations.

item.title: 'Not solely on how much revenue it generates': the UNDP asks the Treasury to shield poor households from the 2027 budget's taxes, as farmers decry the mobile money levy
item.description: At the launch of a 2027 Budget Highlights Report in Lusaka on Monday 16 November, UNDP resident representative James Wakiaga urged government to keep VAT zero-rating on basic foods and to cushion low-income households against higher VAT, a doubled mobile money levy and new tariffs. The ZNFU says it received the budget with 'heightened anxiety'; News Diggers has set out the levy bands and a passport fee rising to K1,000.

item.title: A 54 per cent maize collapse and 23-hour blackouts, written into the books: the IMF credits Zambia with budgeting for climate risk and sets an October 2027 deadline
item.description: An IMF technical assistance report on climate change and fiscal risks, dated October 2026 and publicised by the Treasury on Monday 16 November, says Zambia has made notable progress in writing climate shocks into public financial management. It records that the 2023–24 drought cut maize output by 54 per cent and pushed load-shedding to 23 hours a day, and asks for a quantified climate fiscal risk assessment by October 2027 and coverage of floods and storms by October 2028.

item.title: Ten held and four wanted over a hijacked copper truck: police say the Kafulafuta load was offloaded at a Twapia yard and the driver was promised US$200,000
item.description: Police spokesperson Chipo Kaitisha said on Monday 16 November that ten people, including the truck driver and four employees of an Ndola bonded warehouse, had been arrested over a truckload of copper blisters reported hijacked in Kafulafuta on 9 November, and that four more suspects, two of them foreign nationals, were being sought. The quantity and value of the copper have not been given.

item.title: A TikTok video from September, a charge under the Cyber Crimes Act in November: Ndola police arrest a 35-year-old woman over remarks about the President and release her on bond
item.description: Police in Ndola say a 35-year-old woman from Twapia has been charged with using a computer system to commit an offence, under Section 20 of the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025 read with Section 179 of the Penal Code, over a TikTok video posted on 9 September that they say contained insulting remarks about President Hichilema. She is on police bond and is yet to appear in court; Lusaka Brief is not naming her.

item.title: 'Burundi managed to play when we had huge support, so why can't we play?': Zambia face Burundi at Stade Intwari at 15:00 today with second place in Group I to protect
item.description: Four days after the 1–1 draw in Ndola, the Chipolopolo meet Burundi again in Bujumbura this afternoon. Interim coach George Lwandamina says preparations are complete and the young side is 'in a building process'; defender Mathews Banda says a hostile crowd will not intimidate them. Zambia have four points to Algeria's seven, with Togo on three and Burundi on two.

item.title: Twenty-three tracks and half the industry: Rich Bizzy's 'Africa' gathers Chef 187, Macky 2, Chile One and JK, while Prince Luv and Yo Maps release 'Over'
item.description: Two of the week's Zambian releases lean on collaboration. The Zambia Monitor reports that Rich Bizzy's new album 'Africa' runs to 23 tracks across Afrobeat, Kalindula, Amapiano and R&B with a long list of guests, and that Prince Luv and Yo Maps have followed 'Show Me Love' and 'Imbwa Ndine' with an Afro-pop single about letting a relationship go.

item.title: 'So why should he be dragged into it?': State House says Hichilema will not comment on term limits, as Lubinda demands he rule out benefiting and Musumali calls silence endorsement
item.description: Two days after the Justice Minister left three term-limit petitions to Parliament, State House spoke for itself on Sunday 15 November. Chief Communications Specialist Clayson Hamasaka said the debate belongs to citizens, that the President is focused on development, and that those demanding a comment would cry foul if he gave one. Former PF vice-president Given Lubinda has challenged Hichilema to distance himself from a third term; Socialist Party general secretary Cosmas Musumali calls standing aside indirect endorsement; GEARS wants a referendum.

item.title: Killed before dawn on the Mwinilunga road: Kalumbila District Commissioner Brenda Sankisa and her driver die as a government Hilux hits a truck's trailer
item.description: Police say the Kalumbila District Commissioner and her driver died at about 05:00 on Sunday 15 November when their Toyota Hilux ran into the rear trailer of a truck on the Mutanda–Mwinilunga Road, in Chief Mumena's area about 15 kilometres south of the Mutanda checkpoint. A district messenger travelling with them was injured. The UPND's Kalumbila constituency leadership announced the death on party platforms before the police statement.

item.title: 'Especially our children': in Choma Central SDA, Hichilema tells MPs and councillors that public office exists to improve lives, and leaves a gift the papers count differently
item.description: On the second day of his Southern Province visit, President Hichilema and the First Lady attended a service at Choma Central Seventh-day Adventist Church on Saturday 14 November. He told office-holders to make sure children get the benefit of free education, school feeding and the scrapping of exam fees, and said leaders should read the church's messages carefully. The Times of Zambia reports a K100,000 gift to the congregation; News Diggers puts the First Family's contribution to the building project at K200,000.

item.title: Twenty arrests at a suspended gold site, a deportation after a shooting and 15 held over permits: the State moves on Mpika's informal gold rush
item.description: The Minerals Regulation Commission said on Sunday 15 November that 16 Chinese nationals and four Zambians had been arrested at Muneshi Stream in Chief Mukungule's area of Mpika, where it says mining resumed two months after it suspended the site and the stream is suspected to have been polluted and blocked. Separately, the Immigration Department deported a Somali national on Friday 13 November over a shooting at a gold plant in Kanyelele, and held ten Chinese and five Tanzanians for allegedly working without permits.

item.title: Plant in Kawambwa, wait in Lusaka: the Met Department's first bulletin of the season clears ten northern districts to sow, tells 42 to hold off and warns of a short southern season
item.description: The Zambia Meteorological Department's first agrometeorological bulletin of 2026/27, covering 13 to 26 November and reported by the Zambia Monitor, puts the country at a yellow 'Get Ready' level. Rain since 1 October stands at 125% of the long-term average in Northern Province and 110% in Luapula, but only 63% in Southern, 53% in Lusaka and 52% in Central. Ten Luapula, Northern and North-Western districts may plant now; all of Lusaka and Southern and most of Central and Eastern are told to wait, with little rain expected before 26 November.

item.title: Musonda in the 83rd, then Chitambala with two saves: Zambia's under-23s beat Burkina Faso 1–0 at Heroes and win 3–2 on penalties to reach the final qualifying round
item.description: Trailing 1–0 from Ouagadougou, Chisi Mbewe's side needed a substitute's late goal and a goalkeeper's nerve. Caleb Musonda scored in the 83rd minute at National Heroes Stadium on Sunday 15 November to level the tie on aggregate, and Christo Chitambala saved two penalties as Zambia won the shoot-out 3–2. The reward is a two-legged final-round tie in March 2027 against the winner of Nigeria v DR Congo, with a place at the Egypt 2027 under-23 finals at stake.

item.title: Algeria go three clear while Zambia fly south: the Chipolopolo are in Bujumbura for Tuesday's return against Burundi, with Kings Kangwa back and second place to defend
item.description: The senior side landed in Bujumbura at 12:45 on Saturday 14 November and are based at the Hotel Club du Lac Tanganyika ahead of Tuesday's Group I qualifier against Burundi. That evening Algeria beat Togo 1–0 in Tizi Ouzou through Ramy Bensebaini's 76th-minute header, moving to seven points; Zambia have four, Togo three and Burundi two. George Lwandamina says Kings Kangwa, back from a four-match suspension, is a player who can turn a game on his own.

item.title: Mama G walks the red carpet at Manda Hill: 'The Family Affair', a Zambian drama with Nollywood's Patience Ozokwor, premieres in Lusaka with Lagos, Nairobi and London to follow
item.description: Basali Media and Kazadi Films premiered 'The Family Affair' at Ster-Kinekor, Manda Hill, on Saturday 14 November. Written by Veronica Hachipuka and directed by David Kazadi, the film stars Samantha Zulu as Vanessa Milimo, a single mother diagnosed with stage-three breast cancer, with Patience Ozokwor, known across the continent as Mama G, as Mama D. Ozokwor shot her scenes in Zambia in April and returned on Friday 13 November for the premiere; the producers plan screenings in Lagos, Nairobi and London before a streaming release.

item.title: Three petitions and no sponsor: Mwiimbu says the government will not interfere with calls to remove term limits, and will not say whether Hichilema would sign one
item.description: Justice Minister Jack Mwiimbu told a Lusaka press briefing on Friday 13 November that three petitions asking Parliament to amend Article 106(3), the two-term limit, were initiated by citizens and are not sponsored by President Hichilema, the UPND or the government, which will leave the National Assembly to handle them. Asked whether the President would back an amendment if MPs passed one, he said he could not speak for him. UPND legal chairperson Mulambo Haimbe says the party has never discussed the matter.

item.title: 'How can we be unpopular?': in Choma, Hichilema points to 14 by-election wins, promises a dual carriageway to the south and says FRA money will arrive within 10 to 15 days
item.description: Addressing a public engagement in Choma on Friday 13 November, President Hichilema dismissed talk on social media that the UPND is losing support, citing its sweep of all 14 seats contested in the by-elections of 5 November. He promised a dual carriageway from Lusaka into Southern Province on the Lusaka–Ndola model, said farmers owed by the Food Reserve Agency would be paid within 10 to 15 days, and warned teachers and nurses who refuse rural postings that they risk their jobs. The Times of Zambia and News Diggers reported the event.

item.title: Two per cent of everything: Cabinet moves the NHIMA deduction from basic to gross pay from January 2027, as the Treasury takes on the scheme's K1.7 billion debt and dialysis bill
item.description: Health Minister Roma Chilengi said on ZNBC's main news on Thursday 12 November that Cabinet has approved calculating the 2% National Health Insurance contribution on total salary rather than basic pay, part of a rescue of a scheme he said was set up on flawed financial grounds. The government will absorb K1.7 billion NHIMA owes hospitals and suppliers, pay directly for kidney dialysis that has cost the fund about K400 million a year, and contribute for elderly people who do not pay in. The changes take effect with the 2027 budget in January.

item.title: The raid video stays, two paragraphs go: the High Court splits the DPP's objection in the Mundubile and Zulu bail case, and a defence lawyer says three of the 18 could walk
item.description: The bench of Derrick Mulenga, Davies Chibwili and Ireen Wishimanga ruled on Friday 13 November that the flash disk carrying footage of the raid on Makebi Zulu's home stays on the record of the constitutional bail application by Brian Mundubile, Zulu and 16 others, while striking paragraphs 6 and 21 of their affidavit in reply and keeping 19, 20 and 22. The DPP had wanted all five paragraphs and the video out. Defence lawyer Milner Katolo told News Diggers that Bishop Trevor Mwamba and two others could be released or become State witnesses.

item.title: The court goes to the patient: Judge Mulenga visits Jay Jay Banda at Maina Soko after a surgeon's report of a shattered shinbone, with the habeas corpus ruling still to come
item.description: After the State failed to bring former Petauke Central MP Emmanuel 'Jay Jay' Banda to court, High Court Judge Geoffrey Mulenga went to Maina Soko Military Medical Centre on Friday 13 November to see his condition for himself. Surgeon Dr Charles Mukunta's report says Banda had major surgery on 24 October to fix a severe fracture of the left shinbone near the knee with a plate and screws and must not bear weight on the leg. His mother, who brought the habeas corpus application, says she fears he will never walk again.

item.title: £3 billion in and more promised: at the King's birthday reception Britain's envoy pledges investment for Grow Zambia, and the mines minister asks for help towards 3 million tonnes
item.description: British High Commissioner Rebecca Terzeon told guests at the British Residence in Lusaka that UK investment stock in Zambia exceeds £3 billion, that the UK–Zambia Green Growth Compact has drawn £1.6 billion of UK-linked investment since 2021 and that £15 million for the Zambia–Tanzania interconnector helped unlock US$300 million from the World Bank and the EU. Mines Minister Brenda Tambatamba asked for British money in mining, energy and critical minerals, saying new discoveries, not just bigger mines, are needed to hit the 2031 copper target.

item.title: Chilufya scores, Girumugisha answers, Algeria pull three clear: a 1–1 draw before 44,000 in Ndola leaves Zambia second in Group I, with the return in Bujumbura on Tuesday
item.description: Edward Chilufya's 64th-minute finish from Albert Kangwanda's pass put Zambia ahead against Burundi at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium on Friday 13 November, but Jean Claude Girumugisha equalised nine minutes from time and the Chipolopolo found no winner in five added minutes. Algeria's 1–0 win over Togo in Tizi Ouzou on Saturday puts them on seven points to Zambia's four, with Togo on three and Burundi on two. George Lwandamina said his players failed to reproduce their training form; the squad landed in Bujumbura on Saturday for Tuesday's return.

item.title: Two clear goals or out: the under-23s host Burkina Faso at Heroes at 15:00 today, Patrick Chinyemba's professional debut ends in defeat, and Sporting Lusaka lift the Roberts Cup
item.description: Chisi Mbewe's Junior Chipolopolo must beat Burkina Faso by two unanswered goals at National Heroes Stadium this afternoon, Sunday 15 November, to overturn a 1–0 first-leg deficit and stay on the road to the 2027 Under-23 AFCON in Egypt, which doubles as the route to the 2028 Olympics. In Philadelphia on Friday, Zambian boxer Patrick Chinyemba lost his first professional bout to the unbeaten Santiago Vazquez, the boxing site No Smoke Boxing reports. And at Nkoloma on Saturday, Sporting Lusaka beat Kafue Celtic 2–0 to win the Roberts Cup with nine men.

item.title: No visa, no Puerto Rico: Zambia withdraws from the 75th Miss Universe after its nurse-contestant is caught by US travel restrictions, with Congo out too and Zimbabwe still waiting
item.description: Miss Universe Zambia has confirmed that its titleholder, a 25-year-old registered nurse crowned on 8 October and named by Zambia Monitor as Pamela Mubanga, will not compete in San Juan on 24 November because she could not obtain a United States visa under the Trump administration's travel restrictions. The organisers said her case 'is linked to the United States' presidential travel restriction', not to any personal problem. The Republic of Congo has also withdrawn, and Zimbabwe's Roseanna Hall was still waiting in South Africa.

item.title: 'Zambia does not belong to an individual': the ten candidates Hichilema beat in August sign one statement against removing presidential term limits
item.description: Harry Kalaba, Fred M'membe, Kelvin Bwalya Fube and seven other candidates from the 13 August election issued a joint statement in Lusaka on Thursday 12 November rejecting a proposal, attributed to the nominated youth MP Mwato Kabaso, to abolish presidential term limits. They cite the one-party years, Frederick Chiluba's failed third-term bid in 2001 and the 2024 ruling on Edgar Lungu's eligibility, and call on MPs of every party to defend the two-term rule. Zambia Monitor, the Daily Nation and the Zambian Observer carried the statement.

item.title: The maize money starts today: Moyo says farmers owed for 2025/26 deliveries to the FRA will be paid from Friday 13 November, drawing on K14.7 billion of the supplementary budget
item.description: Agriculture Minister Moses Moyo said in a statement on Thursday 12 November that payments to farmers who supplied maize to the Food Reserve Agency in the 2025/2026 marketing season and are still waiting would begin on Friday 13 November, following Parliament's approval of a K19.9 billion supplementary budget of which K14.7 billion is for the arrears. News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report the announcement; UPP president Saviour Chishimba says institutions that missed earlier timelines owe farmers an apology.

item.title: From an operating loss to K6.3 billion after tax: Kapala hails ZESCO's turnaround on his first visit as Electricity Minister, and the utility's own report trims his K6.5 billion
item.description: Peter Kapala, the first holder of the new Electricity portfolio, visited ZESCO's head office on Wednesday 11 November and praised what a ministry statement called a K6.5 billion profit last year, crediting government reforms. ZESCO's 2025 Integrated Report records a group profit after tax of K6.3 billion on revenue of K32.7 billion, up from K30.8 billion, and an operating profit of K11.2 billion against an operating loss of K8.7 billion in 2024. Customers have grown from about 1.2 million in 2022 to about 1.5 million.

item.title: 'No universal, one-size-fits-all' model: China's ambassador says Zambia's democracy should not be judged by a small number of outsiders, days after the EU's election dialogue
item.description: Speaking at a handover of computers, televisions and office equipment to the Nelly Mutti Crèche at the National Assembly on Wednesday 11 November, Ambassador Han Jing said Zambia's democratic future was for Zambians to decide and that each country may shape democracy to its circumstances. He praised the expanded Parliament for widening representation. News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report the remarks, which land as the government seeks to respond to the EU observers' final report before it is published.

item.title: Forms Five and Six return: Kamboni sets February 2027 for Zambia's first A-level intake, open to Grade 12 leavers of 2024 to 2026, with university entry from 2029
item.description: Education Minister Harry Kamboni announced on Wednesday 11 November that Advanced Level education will begin in February 2027 under the 2023 Zambia Education Curriculum Framework, adding a two-year stage after Ordinary Level. Candidates who sat Grade 12 in 2024, 2025 or 2026 may apply for the first intake, taking up to four subjects from approved combinations across twelve pathways; placement runs from 25 to 31 December. The Daily Nation, News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report the briefing.

item.title: A plea on 24 November and a ruling at 11:00 today: Mundubile and Zulu face the sedition charges without counsel, as the High Court rules on their account of the UN refuge
item.description: Lusaka Resident Magistrate Webster Milumbe refused an adjournment on Wednesday 11 November and ordered Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu to take plea on two counts of seditious practices; when Bonaventure Mutale, Sakwiba Sikota and Chifumu Banda said they had no instructions, he let them withdraw and set 24 November for a possible plea. In the treason bail case, the High Court rules on Friday 13 November at 11:00 on the State's bid to strike five paragraphs and a video from the applicants' affidavit, then hears the bail plea itself.

item.title: Bonds of K538,000 and two Toyotas: the ACC charges a Lusaka Archdiocese priest with concealing K1.5 million it links to a former Community Development officer's K5.6 million case
item.description: The Anti-Corruption Commission said on Thursday 12 November that it had arrested and charged Fr Titus Malama Sande, 45, with four counts of possessing and concealing property reasonably suspected to be proceeds of crime: bonds worth K538,000 at a bank, and a Toyota Hilux and Toyota Dyna worth about K1 million registered in his name but, the ACC alleges, acquired by Veronica Chisanga Kabwe. He has been released on bond and is to appear in court. News Diggers, Zambia Monitor and the Zambian Observer report the statement.

item.title: Fifty-six deaths and 2,658 suspected cases: cholera has added a thousand cases since late October, as the WHO offers help on water and the water minister calls in the NGOs
item.description: News Diggers reports Zambia National Public Health Institute figures of 98 new suspected cases and one death in 24 hours, taking the outbreak to 2,658 suspected cases, 351 confirmed and 56 deaths, with 138 people in hospital; on 28 October the toll stood at 1,622 cases and 30 deaths. WHO representative Dr Clement Lasuba told the Local Government ministry on Wednesday that most of Zambia's diseases are preventable and need more than one ministry; Elisha Matambo told the 65-member NGO WASH Forum that universal access needs all hands.

item.title: Free entry at Levy Mwanawasa and 'an element of madness': Zambia meet Burundi at 15:00 today with the President's tickets in the stands and four forwards missing
item.description: Kick-off in Ndola is at 15:00 CAT on Friday 13 November. The Zambian Observer reports that Sports Minister Likando Mufalali announced the President had bought all the tickets so that supporters enter free, four days after Hakainde Hichilema told FAZ he would buy 'a lot of tickets'. George Lwandamina asked his players for 'an element of madness'; Fashion Sakala said the replacements for Daka, Lameck Banda, Gamphani Lungu and Kingstone Mutandwa are ready. Algeria lead Group I on four points, Togo and Zambia have three, Burundi one.
